P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Not established in detail. Foreign currency can be received into foreign currency deposit (FCD) accounts at banks. The dalasi remains legal tender and domestic transactions should be quoted in dalasi (CBG, 2022). No surrender or repatriation rule for individuals' service income was found.
P1_fx_receipts.note: Only 2022 press on CBG FCD rules captured; no current CBG rule on export proceeds captured on 2026-10-22.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Foreign currency deposit (FCD) accounts exist; after temporary 2022 restrictions on cash withdrawals, the Central Bank of The Gambia confirmed in August 2022 that customers can deposit to and withdraw from FCD accounts in approved currencies.

P3_local_gateways.question: Which local payment gateways can an individual or sole trader use to accept online payments?
P3_local_gateways.answer: Global platform availability for Gambia (Republic of The) (automated collector snapshots, Oct 2026). Not listed: Stripe (merchant sign-up); Etsy seller payments; YouTube Partner Program.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual register a business to sell digital services/products? Simplest legal form?
L1_registration.answer: A sole proprietorship is registered at the Companies Division of the Ministry of Justice (Single Window), using form SWR 3 with a copy of the owner's TIN card. The registration fee is D500, and it can be completed within a day in Banjul or at the KMC branch.

L2_tax_id.question: Tax ID: who needs one, how to get it?
L2_tax_id.answer: A TIN from the Gambia Revenue Authority. Everyone engaged in income-generating activity in The Gambia must register and pay personal income tax, and the TIN card is required for sole-proprietorship registration.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: Income tax on foreign-source income for residents; rates or special regimes
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Businesses with turnover under D500,000 a year pay 3% of turnover. Otherwise personal income tax is the higher of the schedule rates or a minimum of 1% of turnover (audited accounts) or 2% (otherwise). The residence basis (worldwide vs source) was not established.

sources.title: Domestic Taxes FAQs
sources.quote: However, if business turnover is under D500, 000 per annum, then the tax liability is 3% of turnover.

sources.title: Domestic Taxes FAQs
sources.quote: The rate of the PIT is the higher of the applicable tax rates in the 1st schedule or 1% of turnover for audited accounts or (2% of turnover in any other case).

L3_income_tax_foreign.notes: PIT schedule (0-25% 'as at 2018' per GRA brochure vs 35% per Trading Economics) not resolved.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST: rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: Standard VAT 15%. Compulsory registration applies at annual taxable supplies of D2 million; voluntary registration from D1 million. Returns are monthly, due 15 days after month end. A guide applies 0% to exports of goods or services with retained evidence (not confirmed in law). E-invoicing was proposed in the 2026 Budget.

sources.title: Gambia VAT Filing Guide 2026 (verified 25 Aug 2026)
sources.quote: It uses the published 15% standard rate and allows 0% only after the user confirms an export of goods or services with retained evidence.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law applicable to a small online business
L5_data_protection.answer: The Personal Data Protection and Privacy Act 2025 has been enacted; the National Assembly passed it in September 2025 and community sensitisation on the 'newly enacted' Act ran in October 2025. It is overseen by a Commission (the Information Commission ran the sensitisation). Breaches must be notified to the Commission within 72 hours. International transfers rely on adequacy or appropriate safeguards.

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
